## Detailed entries

### Anniston

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-08-18, Anniston City Council unanimous adoption of Resolution No. 26-R-97 (added to the agenda by amendment)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-18` (exact)
- **Duration:** 12 months, effective immediately; council may shorten or extend. Planning Commission to report recommendations within six months.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `al-anniston-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution No. 26-R-97 (temporary moratorium on the permitting, development and licensing of data centers within the city's regulatory jurisdiction)
- **What prompted it:** Planning Commission recommendation; existing zoning does not address large-scale data centers (electrical demand, water/wastewater, stormwater, noise, lighting, generators, neighborhood compatibility). City already hosts a 2 MW colocation facility (FirmFarm).
- **Affected projects:** Existing data centers unaffected unless they cease operations 60+ days or let a business license lapse.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; Resolution 26-R-97 adopted 2026-08-18, effective immediately, scheduled for 12 months (to about 2027-08-18).
- **Outcome:** One-year moratorium adopted.

### Birmingham

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Date enacted:** 2026-03-03
- **Normalized date:** `2026-03-03` (exact)
- **Duration:** 180 days from the March 3, 2026 adoption/vote date, expiring August 30, 2026 (March 3 plus 180 days). WBRC and Birmingham Times both confirm the March 3, 2026 vote date and the six-month term; no separate publication-date lag was found or is needed for this calculation.
- **Current end date:** `2026-08-30`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `al-birmingham-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Birmingham City Council March 3, 2026 agenda, P(ph) Item 1, "An Ordinance to consider a temporary suspension on data centers within the City" [Second Reading], adopted unanimously per Birmingham Times reporting; the city's data center policy page (birminghamal.gov/datacenters) confirms the moratorium is in effect [VERIFY: formal ordinance number not yet visible in Municode or city ordinance index as of 2026-04-29]
- **What prompted it:** Regulatory gap and project pressure from large/hyperscale proposals; city cited need to review zoning, land-use policy, infrastructure readiness, environmental responsibility, neighborhood compatibility, and transparent approval procedures
- **Affected projects:** Applies prospectively to new or expanding large/hyperscale data centers above 20 MW. The Nebius BHM01/Oxmoor project and DC BLOX expansion were reported as exempt because applications or permits were already complete or under review before the moratorium took effect.
- **Detailed status:** Replaced; the moratorium ended at the close of its 180-day term (on or about 2026-08-30) and was superseded by the permanent data-center zoning ordinance (zoning case ZAC2026-00001, 20 conditions for hyperscale facilities) adopted 6-3 on 2026-06-09, which per WBRC took effect when the moratorium lifted. AL.com (2026-09-18) lists Birmingham's moratorium as expired and replaced by the new zoning regulations; the city's data-center page now describes only the adopted zoning rules.
- **Outcome:** Replaced by permanent data-center zoning regulations (ZAC2026-00001) adopted 2026-06-09 and effective when the moratorium ended (~2026-08-30).

### Helena

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-22 (City Council gave Ordinance 1043-2026 immediate consideration and adopted it by unanimous consent, 4-0, on its first reading, per official minutes); an amended version (radius cut from 1,000 to 500 feet) had a first reading 2026-08-10 (a motion for immediate consideration failed for lack of a second) and 2026-08-24; an amendment exempting two previously initiated projects was adopted 3-1 on 2026-09-14
- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-22` (exact)
- **Duration:** 180 days from the effective date (upon publication); may be extended or rescinded
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, general
- **Moratorium ID:** `al-helena-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance No. 1043-2026, temporary suspension on the establishment or expansion of gas stations, auto parts/mechanic shops, automobile or manufactured home dealerships, and data centers (amended 2026-09-14)
- **What prompted it:** Zoning does not restrict certain B2/B3/M1/M2 uses near Highways 17, 52, 58 and 95; need to study appropriate regulation while a zoning rewrite is underway.
- **Affected projects:** Amendment exempts a Highway 58 hardware store/convenience store with gas pumps and a proposed two-bay oil-change facility; no data center project identified.

On 2026-09-14 the council amended it 3-1 to exempt two previously initiated projects; data centers remain covered. Council members said they plan a separate, standalone data-center moratorium.
- **Outcome:** Multi-use 180-day moratorium in force; standalone data-center moratorium planned.
